$comment: Target profile. Copy this file and edit to add a new target plant; point pipeline.json at it.
habitat_note: Subalpine meadows AND open subalpine forest / forest edge. Deliberately NOT restricted to treeless meadow: A. latifolia is common under open canopy, so the vegetation stage scores a band of canopy openness rather than applying a binary meadow/forest cut.
$comment_habitat_model: Which stage supplies the habitat layer: 'vegetation' (Sentinel-2 openness, for meadow and open-forest plants) or 'forest' (BC VRI tree species and stand age, for mycorrhizal targets).

observations.$comment: Only ~6 research-grade A. latifolia records exist in the West Kootenays AOI, so the observation layer is a weak positive signal, never a filter. congeners_downweight lists look-alike congeners whose habitat differs enough that their records should not boost meadow sites.
observations.$comment_baseline: Cells with no nearby record score this, not zero - absence of an observation is absence of a botanist. Raise toward 1.0 to make the layer purely a bonus; drop toward 0 to make sightings closer to a requirement.

aspect.$comment: Preferred bearing in compass degrees. 202.5 = SSW, midpoint of the south-to-southwest window in the spec. tolerance_deg is the half-width of the full-credit arc; credit falls off cosine-wise beyond it. Flat cells (below flat_slope_deg) are exempt since aspect is meaningless there.

vegetation.$comment: Thresholds are tuned against the canopy-openness continuum, not a single NDVI cut. ndvi separates vegetated from bare/rock/clearcut; ndmi carries the canopy-closure signal.

ndmi.$comment: Higher = denser, wetter canopy - conifer canopies hold water and self-shadow, suppressing SWIR. Calibrated against West Kootenays reference populations: valley conifer forest medians 0.303, open high ground medians 0.105.

texture.$comment: Sub-pixel stddev of 10 m NDVI within each 30 m cell. Measured but NOT used for closure: against reference populations open ground came out ROUGHER than closed canopy (0.0353 vs 0.0195), the opposite of the usual assumption, because alpine is a rock/heath/krummholz mosaic while closed canopy is uniform at 10 m. It is also the weakest of the three signals (AUC 0.71), so it is written as a diagnostic layer only. Set closure_texture_weight above 0 to fold it back in.

openness_preference.$comment: Relative credit by canopy class. Open forest is genuinely good habitat for this species, so it scores nearly as well as meadow.

logging.$comment: A regenerating clearcut has the same spectral signature this stage selects for - high NDVI, low canopy closure - so without this it is scored as prime open meadow. Verified visually: the top-ranked sites were sitting on hard-edged cutblocks strung along logging roads. penalty is the multiplier applied to freshly logged ground; it fades linearly back to 1.0 once the block is recovery_years old, by which point the canopy has usually closed anyway.

validation.$comment: Used by scripts/validate.py. The contrast is a congener sharing collectors, season and access bias but not habitat, so beating it means the model tracks habitat rather than where people walk.
